resync_trigger: Review the upstream procedure diff before upgrading regenerator2000 from 0.9.20.

resync_triggers.trigger: The installed regenerator2000 is upgraded past 0.9.20.
resync_triggers.mechanism: Read the new crate's own .cargo_vcs_info.json for the commit it was published from (no guessing at a tag), fetch the five procedure paths at that commit from the GitHub repository, sha256 each, and diff against this manifest's per-procedure sha256 values. Any digest that moved means the absorbed prose at that destination must be re-read against upstream before the upgrade is accepted. r2000-upstream-audit.test.ts's live-gated re-hash check performs the comparison half when R2000_UPSTREAM_CLONE points at a clone of the pinned tree.

AppState::file_info() already computes packer_name and is_packed and throws them away before the handler's json! block. The day either reaches that block, SURF-03's packer finding collapses to a one-field read and its external unp64 oracle becomes unnecessary. Watch by calling r2000_get_binary_info after any upgrade and diffing the returned key set against the seven fields recorded in 19-RESEARCH.md section 2.2(a).

resync_triggers.trigger: A future phase needs an upstream call this manifest currently disposes of as omitted.
resync_triggers.mechanism: Every non-curated call has a disposition_rationale entry below carrying the reason it was left out. Two of them (r2000_toggle_splitter, r2000_set_immediate_format) already name the requirement that would supply their criterion. Adding one to CURATED_R2000_TOOLS requires updating that entry's disposition in the same commit, so the manifest cannot silently disagree with r2000-tools.ts.

r2000_get_disassembly_cursor.justification: Upstream's own text forbids the cursor route in exactly the situation this project's absorbed procedure describes, and this project has no editor cursor at all. The caller always supplies an explicit address, and r2000_read_region (SURF-01, D18-24/D18-25) answers 'read this routine' by range. r2000-tools.ts records the trio as HELD, not unproven (D18-26): the absorption diff produced a caller whose own upstream text says not to use it, so the tool stays HELD and this is the recorded reason.
r2000_get_disassembly_cursor.upstream_citation: .agent/skills/r2000-analyze-program/SKILL.md:74 and :128 -- "**CRITICAL**: Always launch each subagent with an explicit target address ... **NEVER** use the 'current cursor address' or rely on the active cursor location in the editor"

r2000_undo.justification: r2000_set_data_type is idempotent over a range, so upstream's 'if a conversion was wrong, undo it and redo it correctly' collapses to 'set it correctly'. r2000-tools.ts records undo/redo as earning no place under this surface's own discipline even now that a session persists. Omitting it costs nothing and adds no surface.
r2000_undo.upstream_citation: .agent/skills/r2000-analyze-blocks/SKILL.md:85 -- "if a conversion was wrong, use `r2000_undo` to revert"

r2000_toggle_splitter.justification: Future-surface proposal, not a permanent omission, and it blocks Phase 20/21 rather than Phase 19. Without a splitter, two adjacent same-type tables auto-merge into one block, so DECOMP-01's 'every byte is code, byte, word, address, PETSCII, screencode or table' cannot distinguish them and BUILD-02's 'data tables extracted to their own files' has no boundary to cut on. It also biases COV-01's divergence sub-report: r2000_get_blocks 'Respects splitters', so the store side will show a systematic over-merge that must be reported as a named bias rather than instrument error. Propose it additively, in SURF-01's pattern, sequenced so Phase 20 has it.
r2000_toggle_splitter.upstream_citation: .agent/skills/r2000-analyze-blocks/SKILL.md:158 and Pitfall 5 -- "**Forgetting splitters**: Two adjacent byte tables will auto-merge into one. Use `r2000_toggle_splitter` at the boundary."; handler.rs:188 -- r2000_get_blocks's description states "Respects splitters."

r2000_set_immediate_format.justification: Future-surface proposal, not a permanent omission, and it blocks Phase 21. It is the low/high-byte pointer-readability step: "format": "low_byte" / "high_byte" plus "target_address" turns a split immediate load into a symbol reference, which is literally BUILD-03's requirement that every branch, JSR/JMP and data reference goes through a symbol so code can move. r2000-tools.ts currently records 'no criterion in this phase'; BUILD-03 is the criterion the absorption diff supplies. Its upstream implementation is mutating (applies a Command, calls perform_analysis() and disassemble(), pushes a Batch), so if added it must go through the r2000-session.ts FIFO mutex.
r2000_set_immediate_format.upstream_citation: .agent/skills/r2000-analyze-program/SKILL.md:84 and :140 -- "apply low/high byte formatting (`r2000_set_immediate_format`) to any immediate pointer loads"; upstream implementation at crates/regenerator2000-core/src/mcp/handler.rs:1645-1695

r2000_unpack_binary.justification: Explicit omission, permanent. The call is destructive by upstream's own description and by its implementation (the handler calls app_state.load_unpacked_binary(...), replacing the binary in place), and this project has a non-destructive route to the same answer: c64-ram-capture runs the program in the emulator and captures RAM past the decrunch, plus SURF-03's packer-identity finding. The entropy gate upstream wraps around it SURVIVES the omission, because entropy is a field of r2000_get_binary_info's live response and the 7.5 threshold is written into the curated tool description.
r2000_unpack_binary.upstream_citation: .agent/skills/r2000-analyze-program/SKILL.md:31 -- "`r2000_unpack_binary` is a destructive action (clears existing comments/labels/blocks) and may take up to 10 seconds or more"; upstream implementation at crates/regenerator2000-core/src/mcp/handler.rs:844-852
